question: Does the burrower enemy honour the `slow` status contract?
verdict: CONFIRMED ON CONTRACT — the burrower's slow scaling is exact in every state it owns. The round-3 0.699/0.397 is a measurement artifact, mechanism proven.
head: a43cc70017da2d0217353d278bcd868a98d7ec09
instrument: Engine stopped (engine.stop() via __HARNESS__.freeze(); engineRunning:false recorded in every raw file). Every fixed step driven by hand via enemy.fixedUpdate(ctx, 1/60) — no rAF loop, single or doubled, touches any number here. Measured quantity is PER-STEP DISPLACEMENT bucketed by FSM state, never path length. Enemy AND player re-anchored to fixed world points before every step (double treadmill), so all arms integrate from an identical position on identical terrain at an identical bearing; velocity carries across steps so accel-limited movers reach steady state. fsm.t pinned to 0 and cooldowns filled so the state under test cannot time out or be stolen.

analytic_submerged.note: residual is the probe's own toFixed(9) rounding, not a physics error

multiplierRead.contract: STATUS_DEFS.slow.magnitude = 0.4 (Combat.js:27) -> 0.6 per stack; Math.max(0.25, mult) floor (Combat.js:615)

subQuestions.a_submerged_proportional: YES, exactly. Per-step displacement = burrowSpeed * slow * h to floating point at every stack count and under freeze.
subQuestions.b_grounded_chase_proportional: YES at steady state, exactly (5.2 / 3.12 / 1.872 / 1.3 / 0.0 m/s). The desired vector and the max clamp both carry the same `slow` factor, so both the clamped and unclamped regimes scale. The one non-proportional regime is the from-rest acceleration ramp: moveGrounded's accel (26) is NOT slow-scaled, so for the first 3 steps out of rest every arm accelerates identically (0.4333, 0.8667, 1.3 m/s) and the per-step ratio is 1.000 before falling to contract by step 12 (slow x1) / step 11 (slow x4). Benign: bounded above by the clean arm at every step, never exceeds it, lasts <=50 ms for slow x4.
subQuestions.c_round3_numbers: ARTIFACT, mechanism proven — Enemy.js:1481 `const close = e.distToPlayer < 2.5` plus general arrival damping. See burrowArtifact and freeRun20s below.
subQuestions.d_unslowed_movement_paths: TWO found. (1) Enemy.js:781-782 the flyer dive integration ignores `slow` and `freeze` entirely. (2) Enemy.js:871-872 the melee lunge impulse is added unslowed. Everything else scales.
subQuestions.e_attack_rate: slow does NOT affect attack rate, windups, recovery or cooldowns — and nothing promises it does. Measured: windup->attack->recover->chase transitions land on the identical step (31 / 39 / 65) at clean, slow x4 AND freeze.

artifactProof_freeRunningBurrow.method: No treadmill, no pinned timer — the same situation the round-3 and round-4 instruments were in. Burrow forced, player parked at a fixed distance, run until SUBMERGED ends; exit reason attributed from distToPlayer at exit.

dist30m.note: at 30m neither arm can arrive inside 2.4s, the artifact vanishes and path length returns to contract

artifactProof_freeRunningBurrow.reading: The `close` clause truncates whichever arm arrives. At 12 m the clean arm is cut off after 0.85 s having walked 9.58 m while slow x1 runs 1.40 s and walks 9.55 m — path-length ratio 0.996 against a true speed ratio of 0.6047. Path length measures arrival, not speed. The round-4 fixer's unproven hypothesis is CONFIRMED.

artifactProof_round3Replication.method: 20 simulated seconds, burrower free-running, player parked and never moved at 25 m — the shape of the round-3 measurement.
artifactProof_round3Replication.reading: Reproduces the round-3 numbers to within 0.02/0.06 using the round-3 instrument shape, while the same build measures 0.600/0.250 exactly under per-step displacement. The inflation is arrival: the clean arm closes to 13.29 m — inside the burrower's 18 m stand-off ring, where `arrive` damps and the `distToPlayer < stand*0.65` clause reverses it — so its path length understates its capability.

newDefects.title: A committed flyer dive ignores slow AND freeze completely
newDefects.why: The `slow` scalar computed at Enemy.js:679 is applied to `d` at line 764 and to the clamp at 765. The diving branch integrates `this.velocity` — set once, unslowed, at Enemy.js:888 by fireAttack's `dive` case — and never touches `d` or `slow`.

controlledMeasurement.rig: anchored treadmill, identical instance state and identical injected velocity in all four arms, 30 steps

liveUnforcedRepro.method: Blind Shrike (`pest`) spawned 11 m from a parked player, left to choose its own dive; the status is applied on the first step it is committed (step 75 of the free run).
liveUnforcedRepro.note: Cross-arm ratios from this free run are NOT reported as a measurement — the Shrike is `erratic:1` and the arms consume different rng, so their commit geometry differs (the slow4 arm committed from a different height and shows ratio 1.23, which fails monotonicity). The valid claim is the within-arm one: a FROZEN Shrike held speedMultiplier 0.000 for all 45 steps and still travelled 6.71 m at a rock-constant 8.946 m/s.

newDefects.playerImpact: The Blind Shrike is a shipping tier-1 unit (selectionWeight 0.7, packMax 4) whose dive is `suicide: true`. Frost Lattice, Hoarfrost Band, Concussion Charge, Grapnel Tether and the Aegis Emitter dome all fail to slow — or even to freeze — a Shrike that has already committed, for the whole 1.1 s / ~18 m of the dive. That is the exact window the card is bought for.
newDefects.fix: Scale the diving integration by the same scalar the rest of the mover uses. In `applyMovement`, replace `this.position.addScaledVector(this.velocity, h)` at Enemy.js:782 with `this.position.addScaledVector(this.velocity, h * slow)` (`slow` is already in scope from line 679, and is already 1 for a dying unit, which preserves the deliberate corpse exemption). Scaling the step rather than `velocity` itself keeps the dive's stored heading and speed intact for `diveContact`/recovery, and makes a frozen diver stop dead rather than drift.

newDefects.title: The melee lunge impulse is unslowed, so a frozen unit still lunges
newDefects.why: The impulse is written straight into velocity at the strike frame with no `slow` term. It then decays through moveGrounded's fixed accel (26, also unslowed) toward the slow-scaled desired, so the excess persists for ~8 fixed steps.

measurement.rig: anchored treadmill, burrower `rake` (lunge 6), 30 steps (0.5 s) after the strike frame
measurement.clampBreach: a slow x4 burrower peaks at 5.58 m/s against its own slowed clamp of moveSpeed*1.9*slow = 2.47 m/s, a 2.26x breach

newDefects.fix: Multiply the impulse by the live multiplier at the point of application: `const k = (a.lunge || 0) * (ctx.combat?.speedMultiplier?.(this) ?? 1);` then `this.velocity.x += dir.x * k; this.velocity.z += dir.z * k;`. `fireAttack` already takes `ctx`. If the lunge is deliberately exempt as attack follow-through (the same argument the DIE exemption makes at Enemy.js:679), say so in the comment at Enemy.js:870 — right now nothing marks it as intentional.

notDefects.claim: S.CHARGE sets an unslowed velocity at Enemy.js:1424 (`e.velocity.set(Math.sin(e.yaw)*s, e.velocity.y, Math.cos(e.yaw)*s)`)
notDefects.finding: Dead assignment, zero effect. `applyMovement` overwrites velocity with the slow-scaled desired on the very same fixed step (Enemy.js:687-688), because `steer` returns the full chargeSpeed vector for S.CHARGE (Enemy.js:557-564) and line 687 scales it. Measured on Ridgeback Charger, gore, chargeSpeed 26, anchored, full 69-step active window: clean 29.611 m, slow x1 17.764 m (ratio 0.5999), slow x4 7.397 m (ratio 0.2498). Step-0 speeds 26.0 / 6.5 m/s — already scaled on the first step. Duration identical (69 steps) in all arms.

notDefects.claim: The erupt vertical pop (Enemy.js:967, velocity.set(0, 9, 0)) is unslowed
notDefects.finding: True but not a movement contract: it is vertical presentation on the surfacing frame with no horizontal component. Measured vy = 9 under slow x4. Not reported as a defect.

notDefects.claim: A dying unit is not slowed (Enemy.js:679, `dying ? 1 : ...`)
notDefects.finding: Deliberate and documented in the comment at Enemy.js:675-678. Not a defect.
Correct — a slow is a movement tax, not a change to the local value of g. Not a defect.

notDefects.claim: Item-driven displacement of enemies (items.js:1136-1137 Grapnel Tether reel, items.js:1431 Collapsing Well drag)
notDefects.finding: Player-driven pulls, not enemy self-locomotion. Out of the `slow` contract by design.

whyRound4CouldNotReachTheBurrow.finding: Not a product bug — instrument siting. `Enemy.chooseAttack` (Enemy.js:814) requires `this.hasLOS`, and LOS is a real raycast against stage geometry.
whyRound4CouldNotReachTheBurrow.reading: At the 25 m stand round 4 used, the burrower had line of sight 0.1% of 30 simulated seconds, so it never chose `erupt` and never submerged. At 12 m it has LOS 41% of the time and submerges within 66 steps (1.1 s), spending 200 of 1800 steps under the terrain. SUBMERGED is reachable in ordinary play; round 4 was simply standing behind a rock.
